# Shared Payload code

The helpers every collection is built from (`src/platform/payload/`). The rules a module note states (staff see drafts, suggestions wait as drafts, publishes are scheduled) are defined here. In the CMS it supplies the `media` collection and the shared fields and access of the others; what each collection allows is on its page in the [content types](/docs/reference/content-types/README.md). Pure helpers are in the [shared helpers note](/src/platform/lib/README.md); email, the robot check, analytics, metadata and the service wrapper are in [platform services](/src/platform/service/README.md); what a preview copies is in [Preview copy](/src/platform/payload/previewCopy/README.md).

## How the pieces link

- **Review queue:** `REVIEW_QUEUE_FIELDS` (source name and link, audience, review status, `externalId`, `contentHash`) are spread into events and posts. `holdSuggestions` sets `suggested` and a draft on a non-staff create, and staff publishing sets `approved`; Admin's Duplicate clears the status and both ids and keeps source and audience (`reviewQueue.ts`, `src/platform/lib/reviewQueue.ts`, `admin/SuggestionsFilter.tsx`).
- **Access:** `draftContentAccess` gives staff drafts and versions and everyone else published documents; `suggestibleContentAccess` (events, posts) also lets agents create, which `holdSuggestions` holds; `readVersions` is set because Payload's default lets any signed-in user read drafts (`draftContentAccess.ts`, #140). Role checks are in `roles.ts` over the list in `src/platform/lib/roles.ts`.
- **Drafts and SEO:** `draftVersions` (pages, posts, events) turns on autosave and scheduled publishing; FAQ and resources have plain drafts. `previewAdmin` builds the preview address from the slug (`generatePreviewPath.ts`). `seoTab` is the one SEO tab of pages, posts and events, stored under `meta` and read by `generateMeta` ([services](/src/platform/service/README.md)) (`contentCollection.ts`, `seoTab.ts`).
- **Addresses:** the link field stores a reference or a custom URL and a look; `resolveLink` is the one place it becomes an `href`, and `documentHref` the one place a document's address is written: pages at `/slug`, `home` at `/`, the rest under their collection (`link.ts`, `resolveLink.ts`, `documentHref.ts`).
- **Paging:** `keysetSort` and `afterCursor` order a listing by one date with the id as tie-break; `src/platform/lib/cursor.ts` encodes that pair as the opaque "Load more" cursor of events and news (`keyset.ts`, decision 0014).
- **Confirmer contract:** `emailConfirmer.ts` is what [verification](/src/modules/verification/README.md) provides and [contact](/src/modules/contact/README.md) uses; `src/payload.config.ts` hands them over (decision 0008).
- **Title band photo:** `bandBackdropField` is the one `backdrop` group of posts and events (phone, tablet, desktop crops, pictures only) (`bandBackdrop.ts`, `src/platform/lib/bandBackdrop.ts`, #1024).
- **Libraries doing real work:** Payload and its plugins (SEO, redirects, nested docs, form builder, search, MCP), `@payloadcms/db-sqlite` over libsql.

- Roles are `admin`, `editor`, `guest`, `resident`, `agent`; only admin and editor are staff, guest and resident have the same access, and a principal from another collection (an MCP API key acting as itself) counts as signed out (`payload/roles.ts`).
- `isNoOne` refuses every operation, admins included, for a collection only server code touches (`payload/roles.ts`); `serverOnlyFieldAccess` does the same for one field. The test helper `restRequest` (`payload/testing/`) sends REST requests to the real handlers, and `mcpClient` sends MCP calls to `/api/mcp` with an API key, an OAuth access token or none, and returns the status, headers and body.
- `PUBLISHED` filters on `_status` even for a staff caller, so public listings never show drafts; `authenticatedOrPublished` lets staff read everything and others published only (`payload/published.ts`, `authenticatedOrPublished.ts`).
- Payload adds edit locks and job stats with access for any signed-in user and no option to change it, so `restrictEditLocks` (staff) and `restrictJobStats` (admin) reset it on the built config, after it is built (`payload/restrictEditLocks.ts`, `restrictJobStats.ts`, `src/payload.config.ts`). - A create by a non-staff user (REST, GraphQL, MCP, or the Local API with a user) is stored as a `suggested` draft and must name a source and an http(s) source link; any other write by them is refused; server code with no user (the seed) passes. Blank text becomes null, so unique `externalId` and `contentHash` never collide on blanks (`payload/reviewQueue.ts`, `lib/reviewQueue.ts`).
- Admin lists show how many suggestions wait, counted from each document's latest draft, with a filter link (`countSuggestions`, `payload/admin/SuggestionsFilter.tsx`).
- Jobs run inside the app's one process: scheduled publishing every minute (`default` queue, at most 10 per run) and the retention queue every 10 minutes. Payload starts them on the first request through its routes, never during build, and each runner names its queue (`payload/jobRunners.ts`, `retentionJobs.ts`, decisions 0010 and 0011).
- Retention tasks are scheduled hourly; a job left processing for over an hour is queued again, and a failed task logs only its name, the error's name and code (`payload/retentionJobs.ts`).
- `expireCacheTag` drops a tag now, as `revalidateTag(tag)` did before Next 16; hooks run outside actions, where `updateTag` isn't available (`payload/expireCacheTag.ts`). - Rate limits count in memory, which is one process: `SlidingWindowCounter` forgets its least recently used key past `maxKeys`. The key is the first `x-forwarded-for` entry, else `x-real-ip`; direct access to the app could spoof it, so it only keys limits (`lib/slidingWindow.ts`, `lib/clientIp.ts`, #118).
- Dates: `SITE_TIMEZONE` (env, default Central) decides "today"; day-only dates are midnight UTC and show in UTC, other timestamps in the site timezone (`lib/timezone.ts`, `lib/formatDateTime.ts`). A calendar day written `yyyy-mm-dd` is a day, not an instant: `formatDayLabel` names it ("Fri, Nov 13") in UTC so no time zone moves it (#1204), and `formatDayShort` names it without the weekday ("Nov 13") for tight spaces (#1224).
- Messages are whole sentences with `{blanks}`; `message()` throws on a missing value, and durations come in words from `formatDuration` (whole minutes). The accounts keys include the passkey card's sentences (#1314), those for seeing and removing a passkey (#1316), the log in button's label and failure (#1315), the divider line between the quick ways in and the form, and the passkey icon's credit line (#1365), the note for a passkey prompt that ended with none and the offer to add one after a log in (#1364), and the Google card's and password step's sentences (#1338). `retention.ts` and `linkLifetimes.ts` hold the periods two modules share (`lib/messages/`, `lib/formatDuration.ts`, decision 0017).
- Email layout takes fixed paragraphs only, escaped, with inline colors (`lib/emailLayout.ts`, decision 0004). `emailAdapterFromEnv` builds SMTP from `SMTP_*`; with no host, or a bad setting (address, port, half a login), it logs and emails go to the log; with a login it insists on STARTTLS (`email/emailAdapter.ts`).
- Database locks: a write that meets a lock waits up to `SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS` (5 s) before failing with `SQLITE_BUSY`, instead of failing at once. libsql waits synchronously, so the whole app process pauses meanwhile (every visitor request, up to 5 s). The deploy's migration step runs again once after a short wait when it fails that way before any migration began, and never once one has (it may be applied but not recorded) (`ops/README.md`). The timeout is set once at connect and lasts only because the site runs no database transactions (no `transactionOptions`): libsql opens a new connection without it after a real transaction. `src/payload.config.busyTimeout.test.ts` fails if transactions are turned on; then WAL or a timeout on every connection is needed (`payload/sqliteBusyTimeout.ts`, #153, #1147, #1326). Migrations are not atomic for the same reason. WAL mode is not on and is a separate decision.
- Visit counter: the self-hosted Umami script loads from the public layout after the page, never in the admin or a draft preview, only when `NEXT_PUBLIC_UMAMI_WEBSITE_ID` is set (fixed at build) and the site has a real domain; it counts for the site's own hostnames only (the address and its bare domain), sets no cookies, honors Do Not Track and sends no query string (`data-exclude-search`: reset and verification tokens, a sign-up email and search words travel there, so a campaign tag is lost too). The script comes from `stats.<domain>` (`analytics/umami.ts`, `UmamiScript.tsx`, #950). The seeded Privacy page says so; live content is edited in the CMS.
- Likely-human clicks (#975): one click listener for the whole public page, beside the script (`analytics/likelyHumanClicks.ts`, mounted by `LikelyHumanClicks.client.tsx`), sends the Umami event `likely-human-click`, always called "likely human, not certain". It counts a click the browser made for a person (`isTrusted`) on a button or a link to another web site, once per button or link per visit. Same-site links, `mailto:` and `tel:` links, disabled buttons, script-made clicks, automated browsers (`navigator.webdriver` or a headless user agent) and Do Not Track send nothing; Umami's own robot filter still applies, and there is no robot list of ours. The visit's memory is a set in the page, so there is no cookie, storage or identifier; the event holds the button's label (60 characters) or the other site's host, never a path or query. Components are not changed. The seeded Privacy page says so.

- `runUseCase` catches, logs only the error's class name (never a message with an email in it) and returns the fallback; `runAction` turns a throw into a failure code and logs it only when that code is `server-error`, since any other code is an expected refusal (`service/runUseCase.ts`, #521).
- `toObjectPosition` turns an upload's `focalX` and `focalY` (percent, set in Admin on Media) into the CSS `object-position` a cropped picture uses, the centre when unset or out of range; Payload applies the focal point only to its own resized files, so a picture the site crops with CSS, the home page's hero photo, reads it through this helper (`lib/focalPoint.ts`, [UI kit](/src/platform/ui/README.md), #1013).

## Shared pieces it uses

- Payload's own types and plugins, the Nodemailer adapter and the site timezone; modules meet each other only through `src/payload.config.ts` and the pages in `src/app/` (decision 0008).
- Module notes that rely on it: [events](/src/modules/events/README.md) and [news](/src/modules/news/README.md) (review queue, drafts, paging), [agents](/src/modules/agents/README.md) (review queue, roles), [accounts](/src/modules/accounts/README.md) (roles), [UI kit](/src/platform/ui/README.md) (`AdminBar` reads `isStaffRole`).

## Rules and the tests that protect them

- **Roles:** `admin`, `editor`, `guest`, `resident`, `agent`; only admin and editor are staff, guest and resident have the same access, and a user with no role counts as a guest (`getRole`), and a principal from another collection (an MCP key acting as itself) counts as signed out. `isNoOne` refuses every operation, admins included, and `serverOnlyFieldAccess` does the same for a field (`roles.ts`; `roles.test.ts`, `src/payload.config.roles.test.ts`, `src/payload.config.protectedFields.test.ts`).
- **Public lists never show drafts:** `PUBLISHED` filters on `_status` even for staff; `authenticatedOrPublished` lets staff read everything and others published only (`published.ts`, `authenticatedOrPublished.ts`; `accessPolicy.test.ts`).
- **A non-staff create is held:** REST, GraphQL, MCP or the Local API with a user stores a `suggested` draft that must name a source and an http(s) source link; any other write by them is refused; server code with no user (the seed) passes; blank text becomes null so unique ids never collide on blanks (`reviewQueue.ts`; `src/payload.config.reviewQueue.test.ts`, `src/payload.config.reviewQueueApi.test.ts`, `src/platform/lib/reviewQueue.test.ts`).
- **A scheduled publish runs on time and queues are restricted** (`src/payload.config.scheduledPublishing.test.ts`, `jobRunners.test.ts`, `retentionJobs.test.ts`, `restrictJobStats.test.ts`, `restrictEditLocks.test.ts`).
- **Titles stop at one shared limit when publishing,** not when saving a draft (`src/payload.config.titleLimit.test.ts`, `contentCollection.test.ts`).
- **A fact tab's label stops at one short limit** so it fits its button (`src/payload.config.factTabs.test.ts`, `testing/factTabsRequests.ts`).
- **Links, paging, cursors:** `resolveLink.test.ts`, `documentHref.test.ts`, `keyset.test.ts`, `src/platform/lib/cursor.test.ts`.
- **The busy timeout needs no transactions:** `src/payload.config.busyTimeout.test.ts` fails if transactions are turned on; the migration retry is `ops/migrate-retry.test.mjs`.

## Boundaries

- `payload/` is for `data/`, `cms/`, `platform/` and `src/payload.config.ts` only. Nothing here imports a module (`eslint.boundaries.config.mjs`).

[0004](/docs/architecture/decisions/0004-email-through-smtp.md), [0008](/docs/architecture/decisions/0008-compose-modules-at-the-app-level.md), [0010](/docs/architecture/decisions/0010-contact-data-retention.md), [0011](/docs/architecture/decisions/0011-scheduled-publishing-runner.md), [0014](/docs/architecture/decisions/0014-cursor-paging-for-load-more.md).

## Known gaps

- The link field's custom URL is not checked with `isLinkAddress`, and `resolveLink` passes it through as typed; only editorial links and chart sources are checked (`link.ts`, `resolveLink.ts`).
- `populatePublishedAt` reads the request body, not the document, and has no test of its own.
